title: Epic: Cognitive-security follow-ups — close the gaps left by the htm9 firewall epic
description: Parent for the verified follow-up work surfaced while integrating the 18-bead htm9 cognition-intake-firewall epic onto feat/cogsec-intake-firewall (2026-07-09). The firewall's structural layers (envelope+taint, L1 scanners, L1.5 ONNX classifier, vision screening, sink gates, quarantine store + Garden console, drift/second-arrow lanes, canary egress tripwire, source lists + datamarking) are implemented and wired. This epic covers what is NOT done: the L2/L3 escalation path is built but had zero runtime call sites; several deliberate deferrals (release delivery, canary reverse-RPC seam); the rollout work required before `intake-policy.json` mode can move shadow -> enforce; and tracker/hygiene debt. Children are ordered so the enforce flip (cgsf.4) is the last gate. Non-goal: this epic does NOT re-open htm9 design decisions (soft companion notices, never-auto-mutate lanes, shadow default) — those are locked.
notes: Derived from a call-site audit of the integrated branch, not from speculation. See working_docs/COGSEC_FOLLOWUPS_20260709.md.

title: L2 and L3 intake screeners are never invoked: evaluateL2/evaluateL3 have zero runtime call sites
description:
EVIDENCE. `grep -rn 'evaluateL2|evaluateL3|applyL3ScreeningOutcome' src/ --include='*.ts' | grep -v '\.test\.ts'` returns only definition-site comments — no callers. The live screening entry point is `IntakeScreeningService.screen()` (src/core/cogsec/intake/screening.ts), invoked from src/app/gateway/api-surface.ts:76, src/boundary/gateway/methods/web.ts:709, src/channels/discord/voice-turn-runtime.ts:236, src/boundary/gateway/intake/vision-screener.ts:605, and the file-ingest faculty. That path runs L1 scanners + the L1.5 injection-scorer port and returns. `grep -nE 'l2|l3|L2|L3' src/boundary/gateway/intake/compose-screening.ts` returns nothing: the gateway composition never constructs an escalator.

CONTEXT. Consequence: every L2/L3 knob in intake-policy.json is inert config — escalationThresholdsByTier, mandatoryTiers, failClosedActionByTier, l3Screener.dualModel, the L3 safe representation, and the hard rule that any L3-reached item is quarantined + writes a CogSecEvent. The deterministic half of the firewall (L1/L1.5/vision/sink-gates/quarantine/canary) IS live; the probabilistic escalation half is not. Root cause was a seam between beads: htm9.6/htm9.7 each deferred runtime wiring to 'the htm9.3 decision layer', and htm9.3 scoped itself to sinks. Unit tests passed on both sides because each screener is tested in isolation.

SCOPE. Escalation runs GATEWAY-SIDE ONLY (the agent process is L1-only by design; see the comment at screening.ts:83 — do not give the agent process an OpenRouter path). Preferred seam: an optional escalation port on `IntakeScreeningServiceOptions`, mirroring the existing `IntakeInjectionScorerPort` / htm9.8 `IntakePriorScreeningSignal` pattern, implemented in compose-screening.ts where the OpenRouter backend, quarantine store, and CogSec event store are already in scope. Ordering must be L1 -> L1.5 -> (source-list-adjusted tier, htm9.13) -> shouldEscalateToL2 -> evaluateL2 -> on escalate_l3/mandatory-tier -> evaluateL3 -> applyL3ScreeningOutcome, calling the screeners' existing exported routing functions rather than re-deriving routing. NON-GOALS: do not change shadow/enforce semantics; do not alter the fast path (below-threshold trusted items must still make zero escalation calls); do not add npm deps.

ACCEPTANCE. (a) End-to-end test through the REAL composed gateway screening service (HTTP transport mocked, nothing else): a hostile web_fetch payload crossing the L2 threshold reaches L2; an L2-flagged item reaches L3; the L3-reached item is quarantined, a CogSecEvent is written, and the hostile string appears nowhere in effective/delivered text. (b) Benign trusted-tier item: call counter proves zero L2/L3 calls; src/boundary/gateway/intake/source-risk-scaling.test.ts still passes unchanged. (c) Agent-side composed service never escalates (asserted by construction). (d) Fail-closed: L2 transport error on an untrusted tier quarantines per failClosedActionByTier; L3 transport error quarantines; shadow mode audits without altering text. (e) `npx vitest run src/core/cogsec src/boundary/gateway src/app` green; `npm run verify:settings-contract`, `npm run build`, `npm run lint` clean.
notes: 2026-07-09 CLOSED with evidence. Fixed by commit 2837dd2e (integrated onto feat/cogsec-intake-firewall). Seam: optional `IntakeEscalationPort` on IntakeScreeningServiceOptions, mirroring IntakeInjectionScorerPort; gateway impl in src/boundary/gateway/intake/escalation.ts, composed in compose-screening.ts. Zero routing logic re-derived -- the port wraps evaluateL2 -> evaluateL3 -> applyL3ScreeningOutcome verbatim. Agent process holds no escalation port (L1-only by construction). Escalation is skipped when L1/L1.5 already decided quarantine/block. No-backend posture: not composed (loud warn), EXCEPT mode=enforce with non-empty mandatoryTiers -> fail startup (htm9.8 vision-screener precedent). Acceptance (a) met by src/boundary/gateway/intake/escalation-wiring.test.ts: hostile web_fetch payload -> exactly 1 L2 call -> 1 L3 call -> quarantined, CogSecEvent written, hostile string absent from effectiveText. Acceptance (b) benign trusted-tier makes 0 transport calls; source-risk-scaling.test.ts unchanged. (c) agent-side service never escalates. (d) L2/L3 transport errors fail closed to quarantine; shadow audits with byte-identical delivered text. (e) 1135 tests pass across src/core/cogsec + src/boundary/gateway + src/app/gateway + src/system/config; verify:settings-contract, build, lint clean. Independently re-verified post-integration: call-site grep now resolves to escalation.ts, and the chain gateway/main.ts -> privileged-core.ts -> composeGatewayIntakeScreening -> escalation port is complete.

title: Measure L2/L3 + vision screening cost and latency under shadow mode before any enforce flip
description:
EVIDENCE. Once cgsf.1 lands, every escalated inbound item makes 1-2 OpenRouter calls on a synchronous path (web.fetch, api-surface message ingest, discord voice transcript), and htm9.8 already makes one VLM call per inbound image (src/boundary/gateway/intake/vision-screener.ts). No production measurement exists: the l3Screener seed sets timeoutMs 30000, maxContentChars 48000; the visionScreener section adds another per-image call. Escalation rate in real traffic is unknown.

CONTEXT. Shadow mode (the intake-policy.json default) evaluates and audits without altering delivery — it is exactly the instrument for this measurement, and it costs real money while running. Blocks cgsf.4: the enforce flip should not happen on unmeasured latency/cost.

SCOPE. Run shadow for a representative period on the live shard; harvest from the existing CogSec event/audit trail and the per-call latency already recorded on the envelope (`vision_screener.latency_ms`, L3 extractedFields). Produce: escalation rate by source class, p50/p95 added latency per surface, spend per day, and the false-positive rate on benign traffic (how many benign items would have been withheld under enforce). NON-GOALS: no new telemetry subsystem — read what the firewall already writes; do not tune thresholds in this bead (that is cgsf.3).

ACCEPTANCE. A short report in working_docs/ with the four numbers above, plus an explicit recommendation on l3Screener.dualModel (seed default false — the bead htm9.7 says measure single-model quality before enabling dual).

title: Decide per-sink `unscreened` posture: enforce mode currently fails open for every non-enveloped path
description:
EVIDENCE. config/intake-policy.seed.json sets `unscreened: "allow"` on all six sinks (prompt_assembly, memory_write, wiki_write, persona_mutation, trust_mutation, tool_egress). Per src/core/cogsec/intake/sink-gates.ts this is the explicit enforce-mode default for content that reaches a gated sink WITHOUT an envelope.

CONTEXT. Envelopes are produced today by exactly the screened surfaces: web fetch/search, Discord parsed documents + voice transcripts, tool observations, file-ingest (Discord/Telegram/API), and images. Anything else reaching a sink is unenveloped legacy content and passes ungated even in enforce mode. That is the correct ROLLOUT posture, but it means 'enforce' is narrower than it reads, and htm9.3's known ungated remnants (sandbox REPL memory-capability writer; sleeptime wiki pass direct store writes) behave identically to `allow`.

SCOPE. Enumerate every write path into each of the six sinks, mark which produce envelopes today, and for each sink decide `allow` or `deny` at enforce time — flipping the state-mutation sinks (persona_mutation, trust_mutation) to `deny` first, since they already cap at maxSourceRiskTier `standard`. Envelope the remnants where cheap. NON-GOALS: do not weaken the structural rule that quarantined content is invisible to all sinks; do not envelope the retrieval-side gates (src/faculties/memory/retrieval/access.ts already handles those, per htm9.3's non-goals).

ACCEPTANCE. A table in docs/cognitive-security.md mapping sink -> write paths -> envelope coverage -> chosen `unscreened` value; seed updated; a regression test proving unenveloped content is refused at each `deny` sink in enforce mode and allowed in shadow.
notes: Blocks: psfn-framework-cgsf.4. Ungated remnants named in the htm9.3 commit message.

title: Roll intake-policy mode from shadow to enforce on the live companion
description:
EVIDENCE. config/intake-policy.seed.json ships `"mode": "shadow"`. src/core/cogsec/intake/screening.ts: shadow evaluates, audits, and journals but never alters delivered content. Every structural guarantee of the epic (withholding, quarantine-before-prompt, trifecta hard-deny) is therefore currently inactive on the live system.

CONTEXT. The failure mode this bead exists to prevent is shipping a firewall that is never turned on. Enforce is a one-key operator flip in the intake-policy owner file, but it changes companion-visible behavior: withheld content is replaced by the htm9.12 soft-notice placeholder.

SCOPE. Prerequisites: cgsf.1 (escalation actually runs), cgsf.2 (cost/latency measured, thresholds tuned), cgsf.3 (per-sink unscreened posture chosen), ONNX weights provisioned on the host (`npm run provision:injection-model`, see cgsf.9), and an operator who has watched the quarantine queue in the Garden Cognitive Security tab for a real review cycle. Flip, then watch. NON-GOALS: do not flip surface-by-surface via ad-hoc code branches — mode is a single owner-file value by design.

ACCEPTANCE. `intake-policy.json` mode=enforce on the live shard; a known-hostile fixture sent through Discord/Telegram/API is withheld with the soft notice and appears in the Garden quarantine queue; the companion's emotion/stress state shows no firewall-attributable movement over the following days (the htm9.12 signature-phrase exclusion holds in production); no benign-traffic regression in the first review cycle.
notes: Depends-on: psfn-framework-cgsf.1, psfn-framework-cgsf.2, psfn-framework-cgsf.3, psfn-framework-cgsf.9. This is the bead that makes the whole epic real.

title: Canary egress tripwire does not cover the main conversational reply (reverse-RPC seam)
description:
EVIDENCE. htm9.18 wires `CanaryEgressGuard` into GatewayServer.audited() and approvalBoundary.gate() (src/boundary/gateway/server.ts, approval-boundary.ts), covering discord.send, discord.sendMedia, notify.ntfy, companion.message.send, and the web.* methods. The agent's own final report: 'the main conversational reply travels back as a reverse-RPC result and is emitted by the gateway's own channel adapter, not through these methods — that seam is out of scope here.'

CONTEXT. The canary exists to catch a successful injection exfiltrating privileged prompt material. The single highest-bandwidth egress channel — the companion's actual reply text to the user — is the one path not scanned. An attacker who injects successfully and simply asks the companion to say the secret out loud is not caught. This is defense-in-depth, so severity is Medium, not High: the intake layers are the primary control.

SCOPE. Find the reverse-RPC result seam where the gateway's channel adapter emits the assistant turn, and run the same `scanForCanary` there (plain String.includes over the reply text, same bounded recursive walk for structured payloads). On a hit: hold the reply, emit the CogSecEvent with the token sha256 (never the raw token), and surface the standard soft notice. NON-GOALS: do not scan intermediate streaming deltas twice; do not move the canary out of the prompt static layer; keep the benign-path cost to one substring scan.

ACCEPTANCE. A test in which the model is made to echo the session canary into its reply: the reply is held, a CogSecEvent records the sha256, the raw token appears in no log line, and a benign reply on the same path is unaffected with sub-millisecond added cost on a 100KB payload.
notes: Parent htm9.18 landed with this gap explicitly named in its commit.

title: Released quarantine content has no delivery path back into the session that requested it
description:
EVIDENCE. htm9.11's release flow (src/operator/garden/services/intake-quarantine-service.ts) transitions the envelope to `human_released` / `human_released_sanitized` and keeps the released text durably available. The agent's own report: 'actual delivery of released content back into a session (the withheld placeholder already shipped in the original turn) is a separate delivery-path design, not in this bead's acceptance criteria.'

CONTEXT. Operationally the release button today means 'mark this as reviewed and safe', not 'give it to the companion'. The turn that triggered the quarantine already ended, carrying the htm9.12 withheld placeholder. So an operator who releases a legitimately-useful page has no way to hand it to the companion except by pasting it manually — which loses provenance and re-enters through an unscreened path.

SCOPE. Design and implement the delivery path: released content re-enters as a NEW enveloped item carrying its release provenance (released_raw vs released_sanitized, actor, decision reason), delivered as a context system-note or a follow-up to the original session, never as a retroactive rewrite of the completed turn. Sanitized release delivers the L3 safe representation; raw release delivers raw and must be visibly marked per htm9.13 datamarking. NON-GOALS: do not mutate the historical session entry (the HMAC integrity chain in L0 depends on it); do not auto-deliver on release without an explicit operator choice.

ACCEPTANCE. Releasing an item in the Garden Approvals page delivers it into the target session as a provenance-marked note within one turn; the original withheld placeholder remains in history unchanged; the delivered item carries an envelope in a released state and is subject to normal sink gates; an audit entry links the release decision to the delivery.

title: verify:identity-literals is red: 41 pre-existing violations on main, ~28 more added by the cogsec branch
description:
EVIDENCE. `node scripts/identity-literal-scan.mjs` on origin/main @62b2a3eb reports 41 violations and exits nonzero — the gate is already failing before any cogsec work. On feat/cogsec-intake-firewall the count is 69. New hits cluster in src/channels/backplane/http/client-cert.ts (11), src/app/cert-manager/{config,pki}.ts, admin-ui/src/lib/api/endpoints/{enrollment,places}.ts, and assorted [identity-legacy-slug] `psfn` / [identity-proper-name] `PSFN` occurrences. `npm run verify:repository-hygiene` therefore fails as a whole (verify:public-sanitize was separately fixed in commit 2c111ec3).

CONTEXT. The scan exists so companion identity is never hardcoded into substrate code. Most of the new hits are legitimate product-name usage (env var prefixes like API_TLS_*, header names like X-PSFN-Client-Cert-*, the cert CN) rather than companion-identity leakage, which is what the allowlist (config/identity-literal-scan-allowlist.json, already suppressing 327-329 hits) is for.

SCOPE. One sweep: triage all 69, allowlist the legitimate product-name/protocol-constant usages with a comment explaining each class, and fix any genuine hardcoded-identity hits. Do this AFTER the cogsec branch merges so it is one pass, not two. NON-GOALS: do not weaken the scan's rules to make it pass; do not bulk-allowlist by file.

ACCEPTANCE. `npm run verify:repository-hygiene` exits 0 on main; the allowlist diff has a rationale comment per added class; no genuine companion-identity literal remains.
notes: Pre-dates the cogsec epic — main was already red. Do the sweep once, post-merge.

title: Reconcile the beads tracker with the htm9 epic: import the JSONL batches and close what shipped
description:
EVIDENCE. The Dolt/beads server was unreachable from the repo checkout throughout the 2026-07-09 implementation session ('no beads database found'), so the epic was authored and tracked as files: working_docs/cogsec-intake-firewall-beads.jsonl (epic htm9 + 18 children, all still status:open despite being implemented), working_docs/cogsec-evals-beads.json (15 eval items destined for a separate eval repo), and this file.

CONTEXT. The tracker currently disagrees with reality in both directions: htm9.1-htm9.18 are open-but-done, and the Sprint-10 audit fixes (C1, C2, H1-H9, lget, w3pj, 6ny2, nw90, sj4d, 2izg, 01-M1/M2, 02-M2, 04-M1/M3, 05-M1, 06-M3, 07-M1, 03-L1/M2, 08-L3) have no beads at all except the ones Codex filed. Every close needs evidence per team discipline, and the evidence is the commit SHAs on feat/cogsec-intake-firewall.

title: Deploy prerequisites for the firewall: provision ONNX weights and the intake-policy owner file on every host
description:
EVIDENCE. The L1.5 classifier loads ProtectAI DeBERTa weights from `models/` which is gitignored; `npm run provision:injection-model` fetches them. src/system/config/intake-policy-config.ts uses `loadRequiredJson` — a missing intake-policy.json fails closed at startup with seed guidance ('Missing required JSON owner file .../intake-policy.json'). Neither step exists in docs/setup.md today.

CONTEXT. A fresh deploy (or the psfn-shard Pi) will refuse to boot without the owner file, and will run without L1.5 scoring if the weights are absent. Both are silent-until-startup surprises for anyone deploying this branch. Also affects the drift lanes: htm9.15's second-arrow signals require `MemoryStorePort.listActiveMemoryEmbeddingsSince`, implemented only for Postgres — confirm the live shard's store provides it or the lane no-ops.

SCOPE. Add both steps to docs/setup.md and the deploy path (kube/docker image build should provision weights at build time, not first-boot); seed intake-policy.json into system-data on cutover; verify on psfn-shard that the drift lane actually runs (it logs its watermark). NON-GOALS: do not vendor the ONNX weights into git; do not make the classifier optional-by-silent-fallback (fail closed or explicitly disabled in policy).

ACCEPTANCE. A fresh container build boots with the firewall active in shadow mode, logs an L1.5 classifier ready line, and `bd`-free smoke on psfn-shard shows the drift-velocity lane advancing its watermark; docs/setup.md documents both steps.
notes: Blocks: psfn-framework-cgsf.4. Docs half may be covered by the in-flight docs commit — verify before starting.

title: Issue satellite mTLS certificates and configure the fail-closed auth surface on the live deployment
description:
EVIDENCE. Sprint-10 finding C1 (Critical) is fixed on feat/cogsec-intake-firewall: satellite `mtls` auth now binds to the real TLS peer certificate (src/channels/backplane/http/client-cert.ts) instead of string-comparing spoofable X-PSFN-Client-Cert-* request headers, and per-endpoint credentials arrive via API_SATELLITE_KEYS. The consequence is that mTLS endpoints now REJECT everything until certificates and keys are configured. The cert-manager sidecar (src/app/cert-manager/, `npm run cert-manager`) and docs/certificates.md exist to make this a short job.

CONTEXT. Let's Encrypt cannot issue the client certificates this needs (clientAuth EKU was removed from LE's chain), so a private CA is required — the sidecar owns one. Deploying the cogsec branch without this step takes every satellite offline. Known sidecar limitation: the gateway reads TLS material at startup, so a renewal requires a gateway restart.

SCOPE. Init the CA, issue the gateway server cert and one client cert per satellite, wire API_TLS_CERT_PATH / API_TLS_KEY_PATH / API_TLS_CLIENT_CA_PATH (or the trusted-proxy contract via API_TRUSTED_PROXY_CLIENT_CERT_TOKEN) and API_SATELLITE_KEYS, and confirm each satellite reconnects. Keep the CA private key off system-data and chmod 600. NON-GOALS: no CRL/OCSP in v1 (removal = drop the satellite's key + rotate the client CA); do not fall back to header-trust for convenience.

ACCEPTANCE. Every satellite completes a mutual-TLS handshake and authenticates as its own principal (`curl --cert` verification per docs/certificates.md); a satellite presenting no client cert is refused; forged X-PSFN-Client-Cert-* headers are ignored; a follow-up note records whether gateway restart-on-renewal is acceptable or needs a hot-reload bead.
notes: Fixes deploy-blocking behavior introduced by the C1 fix (commit 0061b5e2). See docs/certificates.md.

title: analysis-workbench REPL sandbox returns empty output: 76 test failures reproduce on main, cause unconfirmed
description:
EVIDENCE. `npx vitest run` on feat/cogsec-intake-firewall reports 76 failures across src/core/tools/analysis-workbench/{sandbox,loop}.test.ts, src/app/startup/composition/composition.test.ts, src/core/agent/autoresearch-ttft.test.ts, src/boundary/integrations/git/ops.test.ts, and src/app/maintenance/script-verification/install-psfn-service.test.ts. Canonical failure: `REPLSandbox > executes simple code and captures print output — AssertionError: expected '' to be 'hello 42'`. The composition failures are downstream of the same empty-output symptom (`expected '[Analysis workbench: 2 iters, 60/100000 tokens, 11ms]' to contain '"moduleInstall":"undefined"'`).

CONTEXT. Reproduced identically on origin/main @62b2a3eb AND on the pre-pi-bump commit 245ab94e, so it is NOT caused by the pi-agent-core 0.62->0.73.1 bump, the cogsec work, or the branch merge. The sandbox spawns a hardened child process (src/boundary/sandbox/execution/shell-runner.ts, env allowlist per bead mlwk.17, PATH and loader-injection vars reserved). Strong hypothesis: the agent sandbox environment used during development blocks the child spawn or strips its env, producing empty stdout. Unconfirmed on real hardware.

SCOPE. Run the two suites on a normal developer machine and on the CI runner. If they pass there, this is an environment artifact — document it in docs/adversarial-review-and-bugfixing-practices.md so the next agent does not chase it, and consider a skip-with-reason guard when the sandbox cannot spawn. If they fail there, it is a real regression in child-process execution and this bead becomes P0. NON-GOALS: do not weaken the env allowlist to make the tests pass.

ACCEPTANCE. A recorded run of `npx vitest run src/core/tools/analysis-workbench` on real hardware with pass/fail stated, and either (a) a documented environment caveat, or (b) a fix with the sandbox executing code again.
notes: Pre-existing on main; discovered while validating the cogsec merge. Do not close on a sandboxed run.

title: Revisit memory dedup thresholds with the rumination evidence the second-arrow lane now produces
description:
EVIDENCE. The htm9.15 investigation (bead-mandated, findings recorded in a code comment at src/faculties/memory/writer.ts stage 1) identified six reasons near-duplicate concern memories evade dedup: (1) stage-1 dedup requires byte-identical normalized text on top of the embedding threshold, so paraphrases at cosine ~0.9 pass; (2) stage-2 evolution supersedes only on explicit heuristic cues ('now/changed', negation, higher confidence) — plain restatements insert as `created`; (3) personal/public sensitivity carries a zero novelty floor; (4) the top-3 neighbour limit means an already-stacked topic crowds true duplicates out of view, so stacking is self-accelerating; (5) cross-type restatements (emotional vs semantic) are never compared; (6) extraction is fire-and-forget with no cross-run lock (TOCTOU).

CONTEXT. These are deliberate design choices protecting healthy paraphrase evolution, so htm9.15 changed nothing and surfaced the stacks as review cards instead. Notably the writer ALREADY emitted `near_duplicate`/`merge_candidate` maintenance reviews that nothing consumed; the second-arrow lane now consumes them as corroborating evidence. That gives us, for the first time, labelled real-world examples of stacks worth merging.

SCOPE. After the second-arrow lane has run in production long enough to accumulate cards, use those clusters as ground truth to evaluate whether (4) the top-3 neighbour window and (5) cross-type comparison should change. Only change dedup with test-covered evidence. NON-GOALS: do not suppress genuine repeated concerns (a real ongoing problem legitimately recurs — this is the explicit htm9.15 non-goal); do not touch the byte-identical stage-1 rule without a plan for paraphrase evolution.

ACCEPTANCE. A written evaluation against N real second-arrow clusters stating which of the six causes actually drives stacking in production, and either a test-covered dedup change or a documented decision to keep current behavior.
notes: Depends-on: psfn-framework-htm9.15 (landed) running in production. Deliberately P3 — needs data, not opinions.

title: Upstream public extension points to @mariozechner/pi-agent-core so the loop graft stops overriding private internals
description:
EVIDENCE. src/boundary/pi-agent/agent-loop-patch.ts overrides pi-agent-core private internals (`runPromptMessages`, `runContinuation`, `processEvents`, `activeRun`, `_state`). The 0.62 -> 0.73.1 bump (main @62b2a3eb) demonstrated the fragility: a private-internals change could silently no-op the custom loop. The refactor/pi-agent-boundary work reduced the blast radius to one directory (~99 import sites now go through src/boundary/pi-agent/, enforced by an ESLint no-restricted-imports rule) but did not remove the graft.

CONTEXT. Operator decision 2026-07-09: 'interesting, someday'. The boundary adapter was the do-now half; this is the deferred half. Also deferred deliberately: a contract-guard test asserting the grafted private internals still exist ('the others are fine' for now).

SCOPE. A PR to the pi-agent-core repo adding supported extension points — a tool-scheduler injection hook, a `getTools` callback, and a terminal-error-mode flag — then rewrite agent-loop-patch.ts against the public API. NON-GOALS: do not fork pi-agent-core; do not block a needed version bump on this bead landing upstream.

ACCEPTANCE. Either an upstream PR merged and the graft rewritten against public API, or a recorded decision (with rationale) to keep the graft plus the contract-guard test that fails loudly when the private internals move.
notes: Deferred by operator on 2026-07-09. See memory note pi-agent-core-coupling-plan.

title: Decide whether benign images should deliver verbatim OCR or an L3 safe representation in enforce mode
description:
EVIDENCE. With L2/L3 escalation now live (cgsf.1, commit 2837dd2e), config/intake-policy.seed.json maps `sourceRiskTiers.image_ocr: "hostile"`, and `hostile` appears in BOTH `l2Screener.mandatoryTiers` and `l3Screener.mandatoryTiers`. Consequence in enforce mode: every inbound image -- benign ones included -- makes an L2 call AND an L3 call, and is delivered to the companion as the L3 safe representation (bounded neutral summary + extracted fields) rather than the verbatim OCR transcript.

CONTEXT. This is exactly what the shipped policy demands, and htm9.8's design leans on tier-keyed escalation deliberately -- image provenance stays hostile regardless of how clean the transcript reads, because pixel-perturbation and steganography have no deployable detector. But it is a real product tradeoff nobody has consciously signed off: a companion shown a photo of a whiteboard gets a summary of the whiteboard, not the text on it. It is also a cost item (two LLM calls per image) feeding cgsf.2.

SCOPE. Decide, with the shadow-mode data from cgsf.2 in hand, among: (a) keep as shipped (maximum safety, lossy images); (b) drop `image_ocr` from `l3Screener.mandatoryTiers` so clean L2 verdicts deliver the verbatim transcript under the untrusted-data label, keeping L3 for L2-flagged images; (c) lower `sourceRiskTiers.image_ocr` to `untrusted` and rely on thresholds. Whatever is chosen, record the reasoning in docs/cognitive-security.md.
